    // Complete integer preimage of Vanilla gamma under IEEE binary64 conversion.

    function guardFee(int256 f) internal returns(int256) {

    function isArb(bool b,uint256 ax,uint256 ay,uint256 x,uint256 y,uint256 px,uint256 py,uint256 fb,uint256 fa) external pure returns(bool) {return leanLabel(b,ax,ay,x,y,px,py,fb,fa)==1;}

library TellMath {
    uint256 internal constant WAD = 1e18;
    uint256 internal constant TWO53 = 1 << 53;
    uint256 internal constant TWO52 = 1 << 52;
    uint256 internal constant LIM = 1 << 128;

    /// floor(log2(x)) + 1, 0 for x = 0, by binary normalization.
    function bitLen(uint256 x) internal pure returns (uint256 n) {
        unchecked {
            if (x >= 1 << 128) { x >>= 128; n += 128; }
            if (x >= 1 << 64) { x >>= 64; n += 64; }
            if (x >= 1 << 32) { x >>= 32; n += 32; }
            if (x >= 1 << 16) { x >>= 16; n += 16; }
            if (x >= 1 << 8) { x >>= 8; n += 8; }
            if (x >= 1 << 4) { x >>= 4; n += 4; }
            if (x >= 1 << 2) { x >>= 2; n += 2; }
            if (x >= 1 << 1) { x >>= 1; n += 1; }
            if (x != 0) n += 1;
        }
    }

    /// num/den (both > 0) rounded to nearest-even double m*2^e, 2^52 <= m < 2^53.
    /// One division: the bit-length estimate is off by at most one binade, fixed by a shift.
    function rn(uint256 num, uint256 den) internal pure returns (uint256 q, int256 e) {
        e = int256(bitLen(num)) - int256(bitLen(den)) - 53;
        uint256 sn; uint256 sd;
        if (e < 0) { sn = num << uint256(-e); sd = den; } else { sn = num; sd = den << uint256(e); }
        q = sn / sd;
        // estimate gives q in [2^52, 2^54): at most one step down in precision
        if (q >= TWO53) {
            e += 1;
            if (e <= 0) { sn = num << uint256(-e); } else { sn = num; sd = den << uint256(e); }
            q = sn / sd;
        }
        uint256 r = sn - q * sd;
        uint256 twice = 2 * r;
        if (twice > sd || (twice == sd && (q & 1) == 1)) {
            q += 1;
            if (q == TWO53) { q = TWO52; e += 1; }
        }
    }

    /// e with 2^e * 1e18 <= w < 2^(e+1) * 1e18 (w > 0).
    function binade(uint256 w) internal pure returns (int256 e) {
        e = int256(bitLen(w)) - 60; // bitLen(1e18) = 60
        if (!_atLeast(w, e)) e -= 1;
        else if (_atLeast(w, e + 1)) e += 1;
    }

    function _atLeast(uint256 w, int256 e) private pure returns (bool) {
        return e >= 0 ? (WAD << uint256(e)) <= w : WAD <= (w << uint256(-e));
    }

    function _min(int256 a, int256 b) private pure returns (int256) { return a < b ? a : b; }

    /// log2 of the grid: min(binade(before), binade(after)) - 52.
    function gridExp(uint256 beforeW, uint256 afterW) internal pure returns (int256) {
        return _min(binade(beforeW), binade(afterW)) - 52;
    }

    /// min(1, ulp(paid)/grid) scaled by 1e18, paid = fl(paidW/1e18) (the double behind paidW).
    /// Returns 0 for out-of-bounds inputs. 1e18 means the paid amount is no finer than the grid.
    function ulpOverGridWad(uint256 paidW, uint256 beforeW, uint256 afterW) internal pure returns (uint256) {
        if (paidW == 0 || paidW >= LIM || beforeW == 0 || beforeW >= LIM || afterW == 0 || afterW >= LIM) return 0;
        (, int256 pe) = rn(paidW, WAD);
        int256 d = gridExp(beforeW, afterW) - pe;
        if (d <= 0) return WAD;
        if (d > 64) return 0;
        return WAD >> uint256(d);
    }

    // ---- LEAN TELL of result lb-4 (scratch/LeanTell.sol, functions verbatim): buy-grid's bounded sell_one_division / buy_grid tests,
    // budget 4, in exact integer binary64 (round-to-nearest-even) arithmetic. A double is m*2^e with 2^52 <= m <= 2^53; 1e18 = LT_C*2^7.
    // ltTell returns 0 unsupported, 1 positive, 2 negative, 3 over budget. Mirrors lean_tell.py bit for bit. Credit Taylor (gtmcknight).
    uint256 constant LT_C=7812500000000000;
    function ltMsb(uint256 x) internal pure returns(uint256 r){unchecked{
        if(x>>128!=0){x>>=128;r=128;}if(x>>64!=0){x>>=64;r+=64;}if(x>>32!=0){x>>=32;r+=32;}if(x>>16!=0){x>>=16;r+=16;}
        if(x>>8!=0){x>>=8;r+=8;}if(x>>4!=0){x>>=4;r+=4;}if(x>>2!=0){x>>=2;r+=2;}if(x>>1!=0)r++;

    // n / 2^s to nearest, ties to even; s >= 1.

    // Wad of RN(d*2^e / g), g = G*2^-53, 0 < d < 2^53 exact.
    function ltDivWad(uint256 d,int256 e,uint256 G) internal pure returns(uint256){unchecked{
        uint256 n=(d<<110)/G;if(n*G!=d<<110)n|=1;

    // G = 2^53 * RN(1 - RN(RN(fee)/1e18)), fee <= 1e17.
    function ltGamma(uint256 f) internal pure returns(uint256){unchecked{
        if(f==0)return 1<<53;

        if(sf>52){sf-=52;f=ltRound(f,sf);}else sf=0;
        uint256 n=(f<<110)/LT_C;if(n*LT_C!=f<<110)n|=1;
        uint256 s=ltMsb(n)-52;uint256 r=64-s-sf;

    }}
    // Every double whose wad is w (2^60 <= w < 2^120): mantissas a, b (0 = absent), exponent e.
    function ltPre(uint256 w) internal pure returns(uint256 a,uint256 b,int256 e){unchecked{
        uint256 n=(w<<64)/1e18;uint256 h=ltMsb(n);uint256 m=n>>(h-52);e=int256(h)-116;

        if(ltWad(m+1,e)==w)b=m+1;
    }}
    // Virtual reserves xv = (m+k)*2^e > rx whose amount wad is ax.
    function ltGrid(uint256 m,int256 e,uint256 k0,uint256 G,uint256 ax) internal pure returns(uint256 hits){unchecked{
        if(m==0)return 0;
        uint256 lo=k0;uint256 hi=k0+1;if(k0>>48!=0){lo--;hi++;}
        if(lo==0)lo=1;
        for(uint256 k=lo;k<=hi;k++){
            uint256 t=m+k;if(t>>53!=0&&(t&1)!=0)continue;
            if(ltDivWad(k,e,G)==ax)hits++;
        }
    }}
    // px, py: previous callback's reserve wads; fee: the fee wad returned then for this side
    // (bid when the pool buys X); ax, ay, cy: this trade's amountX, amountY, reserveY.
    function ltTell(uint256 px,uint256 py,uint256 fee,uint256 ax,uint256 ay,uint256 cy,bool buy) internal pure returns(uint256){unchecked{
        if(fee>1e17)return 0;
        uint256 G=ltGamma(fee);

            (uint256 a,uint256 b,int256 e)=ltPre(px);
            if((a|b)==0)return 0;
            uint256 k0=ax*G/(uint256(1e18)<<uint256(e+53));
            uint256 hits=ltGrid(a,e,k0,G,ax)+ltGrid(b,e,k0,G,ax);
            if((a!=0?1:0)+(b!=0?1:0)+hits>4)return 3;
            return hits!=0?1:2;
        }
        if(py>>60==0||py>>120!=0||cy>>60==0||cy>>120!=0||ay==0||ay>>120!=0)return 0;
        (uint256 y0,uint256 y1,int256 ey)=ltPre(py);(uint256 z0,uint256 z1,int256 ez)=ltPre(cy);
        if((y0|y1)==0||(z0|z1)==0)return 0;
        int256 de=ez-ey;if(de>1||de<-1)return 0;
        if(de==1){z0<<=1;z1<<=1;}else if(de==-1){y0<<=1;y1<<=1;ey=ez;}

    // ---- qlite-a split test: qlgate.py cap24+GATE = qlite_int.capped_int(cap=24) in exact integer binary64 (round-to-nearest-even)
    // arithmetic, one candidate (preimage pair (0,0), z = r, k = n). Credit Taylor (gtmcknight), amm-sim 4812a638 research/solved.
    uint256 constant QG=8980177656976769;int256 constant QGE=-53; // 0.997

        uint256 n=(a<<110)/b;if(n*b!=a<<110)n|=1;

    }}
    // RN(RN(w)/1e18), w > 0: float(w)/1e18.
    function qW(uint256 w) internal pure returns(uint256 m,int256 e){unchecked{
        int256 s;(m,e)=qR(w);(m,s)=qD(m,LT_C);e+=s-7;
    }}
    // pw: wad paid; rx, ry: previous callback's reserve wads; fee: fee wad returned then for the paid side; buy: the pool bought X.
    // Outside pw in (0, 2^128), rx, ry in [2^40, 2^128) the answer is a miss.
    function qHitX(uint256 pw,uint256 rx,uint256 ry,uint256 fee,bool buy,int256 m0,uint256 nc) internal pure returns(bool,int256){unchecked{

**Outcome against the requested score.** The supplied starting score is 528.3333 and supplied leader score is 528.4152: the difference is **0.0819**. Under the requester's exact engine-to-board transfer premise, a gain of 0.0819 would tie that score; exceeding it is needed for outright #1. Merely clearing the +0.04 contract-return gate would imply 528.3733, still 0.0419 short of that supplied leader. No measured gain here is approved for that projection. These are the task's pinned scores and arithmetic, not a fresh leaderboard observation.

**Evidence and measurement convention.** Engine edge means the submission arm's score when it runs separately against the fixed 30-bps Vanilla normalizer for 10,000 steps. Candidate, QLX5, and QT1 comparisons use the same seed/configuration, not direct candidate-versus-QLX5 matches. For differences d_i, pooled mean is S1/N and paired SE is `sqrt((S2 − S1²/N)/(N·(N−1)))`, with S1=sum(d_i) and S2=sum(d_i²). No block means are averaged without their sample counts. Adaptive stopping makes the pooled observations descriptive; `mean+2·SE` below is a stopping statistic, not a guaranteed confidence bound. Search arms sharing seeds are correlated and cannot be added as independent gains. [Engine records][root-1-01], [replica records][root-1-02]

**(a) QLX5 + AGE: implemented, checked, and retired for insufficient gain.** The stack changes the nonbinding retail pull, when no split hit occurs, from α=0.35 to `floor(7e17·age/(age+1))` in WAD units, with age measured since the last binding rival observation. Binding bounds and split hits refresh that timestamp; arb does not. The timestamp occupies slot-2 bits 224..254. Existing filter, tell, tables and split logic stay in place. This adds 527 source characters and 118 deployed bytes to QLX5. Taylor's attribution is retained. [Build][b01-qa], [check][b02-qa]

The build's small smokes passed. The subsequent check reported P/T/F passes: on seeds 74200..74249 it compared 549,905 autonomous callbacks and 549,733 fixed-input callbacks with zero reported label/state branch mismatches. Fee checks covered 100,000 callbacks per stream; maximum reported errors were 6.0834e-10 bps and 8.254e-11 bps, below 0.01 bps. Its G field covered size, not an independent engine gas replay. Later engine blocks supplied measured gas/OOG evidence. Candidate Q was cancelled; neither Q nor E should be inferred from the check's `all=pass`. One source flag attaches to that check; the failed quotation is not identified. [Check][b02-qa], [evidence qualification][root-1-01]

**(b) Engine-faithful replica: the useful positive deliverable.** The work corrected much more than constant K: every quote and arb-size calculation recomputes K from rounded reserves; it preserves binary64 operation order, arb caps/profit tests and requoting, incremental fee/reserve accounting, both pools' ordering, pre-callback split decisions, dust thresholds, and WAD conversions. The key additional defect was the exponential implementation in retail LogNormal/Poisson draws. Price GBM uses host exp, but the audited retail stream required the Rust libm/fdlibm path. The original r3/r4 constant-fee cores achieved only 16/128 bit-identical scores, despite maximum relative error 5.943033337599645e-11. r1/r2's corrected cores reported 128/128 exact constant-fee runs. Such small constant-policy error was not sufficient evidence for QLX5: the corrected dynamic policy is sensitive to low bits in fills. [Core comparison][root-1-01]

The four initial policy ports compared 512 saved rows per policy at six-decimal precision. Their maximum QLX5 discrepancy, 4.994752202946984e-7, was consistent with rounded input rows; those tests alone did **not** prove the requested 1e-8 dynamic parity. The later audit reran the release engine with unrounded outputs and reported **512/512 bit-identical QLX5 scores, maximum error 0**, seeds **10010512..10011023**, and **5,626,901 callbacks**. Separately, four proof seeds × three policies produced **1,348,988 trace comparisons with zero mismatches**, covering RNG/orders, routing/fills, reserves, fees, state and accounting. That is the evidence for using the corrected replica. [Unrounded audit][b13-r3]

The audit's negative control is consequential: switching retail exp back to host exp changes an order by one ULP at seed 9700000, step 6. QLX5 then accumulates 57,722 trace mismatches and an engine-minus-port edge difference of 0.03738953382651289 on that proof seed. This is why the older constant-K fast LEAN replica and uncorrected cores must not supply QLX5 efficacy claims. It is a demonstrated sensitivity, not a forecast of profitable strategy changes. **Source limitations and reconciliations.** Source flags mean some cited material failed the plane's reread checks; the precise failed URLs/passages were not supplied. They weaken external attribution claims and cannot be erased by a worker's assertion that it rechecked its own citations. They do not, by themselves, identify a numerical falsification in the embedded rows. The AGE check, several core/port/audit sources, all seven nonempty wide AGE blocks, all c3 searches, eight of nine supplied c4 searches and split-truth carry such flags. The independent Cython check, level-curve and arb-truth are unflagged. The [first][root-1-01] and [second][root-1-02] root merges retain the detailed flag lists.

This report corrects four overbroad readings of the second merge: oracle interventions are not headroom caps; some c4 variants were compiled; repaired-model tuning was attempted but yielded no candidate; and AGE is already retired by the engine evidence in the first merge. Its statements that report seeds were unopened and no engine seeds were run apply to its c3/c4 search/probe results, not to the older idea sweep or AGE/coarse-engine work. No absence of a result is treated as a measured zero.

**Local checks for this deliverable.** The thirteen supplied artifact digests matched their stated SHA-256 values and the JSON artifacts parsed. The archived QLX5 block decoded to exactly the pinned 47,230-byte source/hash, without changing its credit or tables. The AGE payloads were fetched from the content-addressed links in the supplied first merge, decoded as data, checked for unique seeds and a consistent candidate source, and all 1,280 completed three-arm pairs recomputed. All 34 c4 arm statistics, both oracle statistics, overlapping baseline bits and terminal stopping rounds were also recomputed. Payload checksums were checked where supplied. No artifact's embedded program was executed. These checks validate this report's extraction and arithmetic; **no Solidity compilation, engine simulation, or behavioral certification was rerun for this write-up**. Observed gas and parity remain attributed worker measurements.

The report contains its own complete baseline source and all outcome-critical figures; removed `.imd/reads` paths are not needed to read it. Linked payloads retain detailed reproducibility evidence. No dependency was installed for the write-up. No replacement strategy was deployed, and no leaderboard submission was made. **The requester must ask the user before any future submission.**
